clue.text: Reversing, park. What, in a rage?

indicators.note: placed at the head of the clue, it tells us to read the park-and-what pair from right to left

parts.note: to park a thing is to put it somewhere
eh? is a casual way of saying what?

explanation.surface: A driver parking badly hears someone shout, wondering why they are so furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' turns PUTEH round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worked up and agitated is described by this informal phrase meaning in a rage.

clue.text: Corner area in piles of wood

indicators.note: the corner-and-area pair sits inside the word for piles

parts.note: piles of something means many of them
to corner something, as all the supply, is to hog it

explanation.surface: A timber yard has stacks of logs filling one corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown tropical hardwood prized for furniture, so a kind of wood.

clue.text: Girl comes in making sweeping statement

indicators.note: the girl's name enters the middle of the word for making

parts.note: making or producing something is its generation
Lisa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman arrives and declares something broad and unqualified.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad claim stretched across many cases, i.e. a sweeping statement, is a synonym.

clue.text: Of course Tory is by end of conference in command

indicators.note: only the final letter of conference is wanted here

parts.note: of course! is an emphatic yes
Tories are the political right in Britain

explanation.surface: A Conservative delegate agrees enthusiastically as the party conference closes.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of conference, E, comes first; 'is by' just sets the two words beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill order on parade telling troops to turn their heads to the right, so a command.

clue.text: Band lacking time to make comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the lacking-plus-time word is read backwards

parts.note: poor means lacking, as in poor in resources

explanation.surface: A pop group short of time tries to stage its return.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people or soldiers, so a band in the sense of a company.

clue.text: A son impressed by brother's complaint

indicators.note: pressed into means the pair goes inside the exclamation

parts.note: brother! and my! are both cries of surprise; the 's is is, a link
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy is moved by his sibling's grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment, the medical sense of complaint.

clue.text: Cause of skin infection in long article with conclusion at the start

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

indicators.note: the last letter of the article word is moved to the front

parts.note: an item is an article, as in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A lengthy newspaper piece about a rash, beginning with its ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with conclusion at the start' moves the M of ITEM to the front, giving MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny parasite burrowing under the skin causes scabies, so it is a cause of infection.

clue.text: Colour of bottle, say, behind heater perhaps

indicators.note: the bottle word follows the heater word

parts.note: heater is old gangster slang for a gun

indicators.note: say means the word for bottle is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bottle means courage or mettle

explanation.surface: Someone describes the shade of a bottle standing behind a radiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heater perhaps' points at the gangster slang for a pistol, not a radiator.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull bluish-grey shade named after bronze alloy, used as a colour name.

clue.text: Small boy raving about mild expletive

indicators.note: turned about, the whole run of boy-plus-raving is read backwards

parts.note: Tim is a short boy's name, as in Tiny Tim
raving means mad

explanation.surface: A little lad is ranting while letting slip a gentle swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TIMMAD round as a single run.
explanation.definitionFit: A softened form of damn it, said in annoyance, so a mild oath.

clue.text: "Army" crook with extremely evil weapon

indicators.note: taking the extremes of evil means its first and last letters

parts.note: a bow is a weapon for shooting arrows

explanation.surface: A villainous soldier wields a nasty weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: '"Army" crook' is a pun: the crook (bend) of the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The bend in the arm is a joint, punningly an arm-y crook.

clue.text: Broadcast of tape shows where workers may be exploited

indicators.note: broadcast scatters the letters of the two words widely into a new order

explanation.surface: An exposé tape is aired showing workplace abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory where labourers toil long hours for little pay is a place of exploitation.

clue.text: Doctor annoys married English chaps in the main

indicators.note: doctoring something tampers with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic irritates wedded Englishmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'married' is used whole here, not as M.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is the sea, and junior sailors ranking below able seamen are its chaps.

clue.text: Not a word associated with a coloured sort of leather

parts.note: sh! is a call for silence, telling someone not to say a word
green is a colour

explanation.surface: Silence is maintained about a dyed hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough untanned leather, often dyed green, is a kind of leather.

clue.text: Lag (a recidivist primarily) imprisoned by judge

indicators.note: locked inside the judge word, the other letters are enclosed

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of recidivist

explanation.surface: A repeat offender is jailed once again by the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' wants to be a convict, the surface sense; it is the verb, to linger.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger or dawdle behind is to lag, a synonym.

clue.text: Confused person who embraces assailant

parts.note: one who hugs is a hugger
a mugger is a street attacker

explanation.surface: A bewildered man hugs the robber who attacked him.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled or disorderly, so a jumbled state is confused.

clue.text: Charged for present, possibly

definitions.meaning: a charged atmosphere is a strained one
the present is one grammatical form of a verb by time

explanation.definitionFit: Means both strained, i.e. charged, and the grammatical category the present is an example of.

clue.text: Bird emerging from shell, the head looking different

indicators.note: the first letter of the shell word is changed for another

parts.note: a shell is a cartridge for a gun

explanation.surface: A chick hatches, looking odd about the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the head looking different' replaces the C at the front of CARTRIDGE with P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump game bird, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Evil old lady having row on radio

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old lady

indicators.note: radio means the word is heard, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: A wicked old woman quarrels on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line, sounding like LIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means harmful or wicked, so evil.

clue.text: Pause one needed in explosive situation

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the word for situation

parts.note: a state is a situation, as in a state of affairs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In a volatile situation, someone needs a moment to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver and hold back before acting is to pause.

clue.text: Do you understand message title's conveying?

indicators.note: the words carry the answer inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a message's heading has got its point across.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal question checking whether someone has grasped a point or joke.

clue.text: Engineer losing me introducing initially one new term

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the extra letter
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of one

explanation.surface: An engineer drops out while a new recruit is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' turns LOSINGME into NELOGISM, and 'introducing' puts the O of one inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly coined word or expression is a new term.

clue.text: Millions from Asian capital city welcoming sort of writer

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the others between them
capital means the first letter of Asian

parts.note: NY is short for New York city
pretty means somewhat, rather or sort of
a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: Millions travel from an Asian capital to a city that welcomes a type of author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian capital city' looks like Tokyo or Delhi; it is A plus NY, holding PRETTY PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means a large sum of money, loosely millions.

clue.text: I must leave girl behind sadly to become a high flyer

indicators.note: the letter I is to be taken out of the anagram pool
sadly is an anagram signal meaning the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man laments leaving his girlfriend behind to become a success.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of 'girl behind', less I, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lindbergh made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight, literally a high flyer.

clue.text: Animating force and skill possessed by this man on strike

parts.note: he refers to this man
art means skill
to strike is to beat

explanation.surface: A worker on strike shows his animating spirit and skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessed by' and 'on' just place the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulse of the heart drives a body, so it is the animating force or vital centre.

clue.text: Outlaw in tears wasted poison

indicators.note: the outlaw word sits inside the rearranged letters
wasted means ruined, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A criminal in tears is ruined by poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges the tears into RATSE; 'in tears' looks like crying but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat poison, so it is a poison.

clue.text: Explanation covers name abbreviated by a North African

indicators.note: the explanation word wraps around the abbreviated name

parts.note: a key explains, as for a map
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An explanation covers a shortened name next to a man from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North African' looks like one phrase; North is N, and African alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Kenya is an East African.

clue.text: Force Republican to infiltrate party branch?

indicators.note: the Republican letter gets inside the party word

parts.note: a wing is a section of a party

explanation.surface: A Republican is forced to infiltrate a party branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring something out of someone is to force or extract it.

clue.text: Poet in residence originally

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of residence

explanation.surface: A poet in residence at a university, originally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link here: home means in, as in 'is she home?'
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek poet credited with the Iliad and Odyssey.
